candidateAnswers.argumentAgainst: It needs bytes this repository's containers cannot fetch: bea.gov and huduser.gov are refused by the build network, and the director's own download failed DNS. Someone with ordinary web access has to place the files in the Drive exchange.
candidateAnswers.argumentFor: It is the fallback DEPTH2 itself prescribes: show the latest edition that was already out. With the November 14, 2024 county personal income edition (describing 2023) a January 2026 life would see county income from its first day instead of waiting for February 5.

candidateAnswers.argumentAgainst: Every January opening keeps its county income and price levels blank for five to seven weeks, and unemployment and income limits stay blank until September.
candidateAnswers.argumentFor: It is what ships now and it is correct: nothing is shown before its release.

notes: Built toward DEPTH2 A11 on the every-town branch off main 5b5cb4b9. The locked tables state their own editions, read from the bytes: CAINC1 'Last updated: February 5, 2026', SARPP and MARPP 'Last updated: February 19, 2026'. The FY2025 Fair Market Rent workbook was built 2024-06-28, before the August 14, 2024 notice, so it is the original edition. Those four now carry their release dates and the compiler refuses a table whose own edition line disagrees.

Measured in the browser: a life opening January 5, 2026 in Boise City ID, Sioux Center IA and Truth or Consequences NM now shows the two-bedroom Fair Market Rent from day one. County income appears on February 5.

Still withheld until the retrieval date 2026-09-03, because no release date is established: HUD FY2025 Section 8 income limits (effective 2025-04-01, posting date unknown) and the BLS LAUS series, whose months each have their own release.

A separate gap found on the same walk: Presque Isle ME gets no rents at all. In New England HUD files Fair Market Rents by county subdivision (hudFipsCode = county + town code, for example 2300300800 Allagash town), not county + 99999, and the game holds no sourced place-to-county-subdivision relation, so matching by town name would be the inference the binding refuses. A Census place-to-county-subdivision relationship file would close it for all six New England states.
question: The game now shows each economic figure from the day its edition was published, per DEPTH2. The editions it holds are the newest: county personal income released February 5, 2026 and price parities released February 19, 2026. So a life opening January 5, 2026 sees no county income for five weeks, although an earlier edition (November 14, 2024, describing 2023) was out. Can the earlier editions be supplied as files, together with the LAUS monthly release dates for the locked months, the posting date of HUD's FY2025 income limits, and a Census place-to-county-subdivision relationship file for New England so rents reach towns there?

title: Earlier economic editions, LAUS release dates, and New England rents
usableAnswer: Files in the Drive exchange: the BEA CAINC1 zip as released November 14, 2024 (and the RPP edition current on January 5, 2026 if earlier than February 19, 2026), each with its release date; a list of LAUS release dates for the locked months; HUD's FY2025 income limits posting date with its source; and the Census place-to-county-subdivision relationship file for CT, ME, MA, NH, RI and VT.
whyItMatters: Without them a January opening shows only rents for its first five weeks, unemployment never appears before September, and no town in New England sees rents at all.
